clause.text: 1. Form of Sponsorship. During the term of this Agreement, Tickets shall be MP3.com's exclusive partner/source for sports, entertainment, and travel tickets, and MP3.com shall include a Tickets Portal on the "Music" page and the "Pop," "Rock" and "Alternative" genre pages on the Website. A "Portal" is defined as a web graphic with the dimensions not to exceed 125 x 125 pixels and 20Kb in size. The content of the Portal shall be supplied by Tickets and shall conform with reasonable technical and content specifications supplied by MP3.com.

reviews.rationale: The clause establishes an exclusive partnership and portal specifications, but it does not conflict with or alter any of the company’s existing playbook policy positions. 1) It contains no reference to governing law or jurisdictional issues, so it does not contradict the [governing-law-and-venue] playbook: This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of New York, without regard to its conflict of laws rules, and the parties submit to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York. 2) It does not invoke confidentiality obligations or disclosures that would breach the [confidentiality-mutual] playbook: Each party shall keep the other party's Confidential Information confidential, use it only to perform this Agreement, and protect it with at least the care it uses for its own confidential information. These obligations do not apply to information that is or becomes public through no fault of the receiving party, was already known to it, or is independently developed by it. 3) The clause is unrelated to revenue sharing calculations, hence it does not contradict the [revenue-share-defined] playbook: Any revenue or profit share payable under this Agreement shall be calculated on net revenue actually received, at the percentage stated in the Order Form, and shall be payable within thirty (30) days of the end of each calendar quarter together with a statement showing the calculation. 4) It does not impose any minimum purchase or volume commitment, so it is consistent with the [no-minimum-commitment] playbook: Customer is under no obligation to purchase any minimum quantity, value or share of its requirements under this Agreement, and shall pay only for the Services it actually orders. Because the clause does not conflict with or deviate from any of the above positions, its contractual risk is assessed as low.

reviews.rationale: The clause restricts Tickets’ right to terminate to only the first 60 days after the Effective Date, whereas the playbook allows either party to terminate for convenience with thirty‑day notice at any time. This limits the company’s flexibility and increases the risk of remaining bound beyond the desired period, so the termination provision is higher risk. The renewal provision allows Tickets to renew unilaterally and sets an unspecified percentage increase, which is inconsistent with the playbook’s opt‑in renewal and five‑percent cap. Because both the termination and renewal terms are less protective than the playbook standards, the overall risk level is high.

5. Measurement. Upon request, Tickets shall have access to pertinent statistics related to Impressions covering the period of this contract. Tickets agrees to accept MP3.com's measurement of Impressions (the "Count") according to MP3.com's logs and other tracking devices and/or software MP3.com may use, provided however, that Tickets shall have the right to audit MP3.com's records in this regard. If Tickets reasonably disputes the Count pursuant to this Agreement, then Tickets shall have the right to select the independent auditor of its choice to conduct an audit of MP3.com's records (the "Audit"). The Audit will be conducted in such a way so as not to interfere to any material extent with MP3.com's operations. If, for any applicable period, the independent auditor determines that MP3.com overstated the Count by more than five percent (5%), than MP3.com shall pay the cost of the Audit and shall refund Tickets the difference between the amount originally paid and the amount which should have been paid, or MP3.com shall credit the appropriate amount of Impressions to Tickets' account.

reviews.rationale: The clause requires each party to provide broad representations and warranties—including non‑infringement, compliance with all laws, and non‑obscenity—and to defend, indemnify and hold harmless the other party for any breach of these warranties or for all losses arising therefrom, without any limitation on liability. This deviates from the playbook’s mutual‑indemnity preferred language, which limits indemnification to claims arising from a party’s breach or negligence and expressly subjects it to the Agreement’s limitations of liability. The absence of any cap or limitation increases exposure to potentially unlimited damage awards, significantly elevating risk.
